 ASHEVILLE, N.C. (WLOS) — A map documenting the original Mason-Dixon Line sold for $950,000 at an auction in Asheville on Thursday.
 With a 25% buyer’s premium, the buyer will pay nearly $1.2 million, according to the auction. The map was last sold in 1982 for $360,000.
 Drawn between 1767 and 1768, the map shows the boundary between Pennsylvania and Maryland. The line became a lasting symbol of division in the years leading up to the Civil War.
 “We’re a big, big melting pot,” said Lauren Brunk, vice president of Brunk Auctions. “And this line is something that was a big division in the past, less so now, thankfully.”

 The document’s history also prompted questions about political divisions today.
 Chris Cooper, a political scientist at Western Carolina University, said political and cultural identities have become more closely aligned, making cross-party conversations harder.
 “People’s political camps and people’s cultural camps are increasingly the same thing,” Cooper said.
 He described the country as deeply divided, while noting that today’s divisions are different from those that led to the Civil War.
